Rashi on Keritot 12a:10:1.hebrew: והתודה - אשר חטא עליה, גבי טומאת מקדש כתיב בויקרא:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:10:1.english: That he shall confess - "that wherein he has sinned" — [it] is written in Leviticus regarding impurity of the Temple.

Rashi on Keritot 12a:12:1.hebrew: מודים חכמים לר' יהודה - ופליגי אדר"מ בחלבין, כגון: "אכלת חלב", והוא אומר: "לא אכלתי"; ובביאת מקדש, אמרו לו: "נכנסת למקדש טמא", והוא אומר: "לא נכנסתי":
Rashi on Keritot 12a:12:1.english: The Sages concede to Rabbi Yehuda - And they disagree with Rabbi Meir regarding [forbidden] fats — for example, [witnesses say,] "You ate forbidden fat," and he says, "I did not eat [it]" — and regarding entering the Temple, [where] they said to him, "You entered the Temple [while] ritually impure," and he says, "I did not enter."

Rashi on Keritot 12a:12:2.hebrew: אבל בטומאה - כגון היכא דאמר "לא נטמאתי", לא מודו ליה, ולא סבירא להו דפטור. אלמא טעמייהו דרבנן משום מיגו דמיתריץ דיבוריה, כגון: "לא עשיתי שוגג אלא מזיד". אבל גבי "לא נטמאתי", דליכא למימר "לא נטמאתי", לא מודו לר' יהודה. ואיפשיט בעיין דטעמא משום מיגו, ותו לא מידי:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:12:2.english: But with regard to ritual impurity - For example, where he says, "I did not become impure," they do not concede to him, and they do not hold that he is exempt. Evidently, the Rabbis' reason is because of a migo, as his statement can be reconciled [to mean], for example, "I did not do [it] unwittingly, rather intentionally." But regarding "I did not become impure," where one cannot say "I did not become impure" [with such a migo], they do not concede to Rabbi Yehuda. Thus, our dilemma has been resolved [to show] that the reason is because of a migo, and nothing more.

Rashi on Keritot 12a:3:1.hebrew: אדם נאמן על עצמו - בדברים שיש בהם כפרה, לא מימנע לאיתויי חטאת להתכפר נגד קונו:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:3:1.english: A person is deemed credible about himself - In matters that involve atonement, he does not refrain from bringing a sin-offering to atone before his Maker.

Rashi on Keritot 12a:3:2.hebrew: מיגו דאי בעי כו' - אם היה רוצה לשקר, יכול לומר "מזיד הייתי", ומה שאמרתי "לא אכלתי" — לא אכלתי שוגג, אלא מזיד:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:3:2.english: Since if he wished, etc. - If he wanted to lie, he could say, "I acted intentionally"; and [as for] what I said, "I did not eat," [he means,] "I did not eat unwittingly, rather intentionally."

Rashi on Keritot 12a:4:1.english: Regarding ritual impurity - For example, [witnesses] said to him, "You became ritually impure and immediately entered the Temple."

Rashi on Keritot 12a:5:1.english: Old impurity - Yesterday you became impure, and today you entered [the Temple].

Rashi on Keritot 12a:5:2.hebrew: טומאה חדשה - ליכא משום מיגו, ד"טבלתי" ליכא למימר, דהאמרו לו: בשעת טומאה נכנסת, ואי נמי טבלת, לא העריב שמשך; וטבול יום הנכנס למקדש בשוגג חייב חטאת, כדאמר במנחות בהקומץ רבה (מנחות דף כז:): מחוסר כיפורים שנכנס למקדש חייב חטאת, ואין צריך לומר טבול יום. וליכא למימר נמי "מזיד", דבעי' דליתרץ דיבוריה; ואי הוה אמר להו "לא נכנסתי", הוה מתרץ דיבוריה: לא נכנסתי שוגג אלא מזיד. אבל כיון דאמר להו "לא נטמאתי", כי אמר נמי: לא נטמאתי שוגג אלא מזיד, לא מיפטר מקרבן, דטומאה לא איכפת לן אי שוגג אי מזיד הוה, דביאת מקדש הואי שוגג:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:5:2.english: New impurity - There is no [exemption] due to miggo, for he cannot say "I immersed," since they said to him: "You entered [the Temple] at the time of [your] impurity, and even if you immersed, your sun had not yet set"; and a tevul yom [one who immersed that day and awaits sunset] who enters the Temple unwittingly is liable [to bring] a sin-offering, as it is stated in Menachot, in [the chapter] HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 27b): "One who lacks atonement [i.e., has not yet brought his required offerings] who enters the Temple is liable [to bring] a sin-offering, and needless to say a tevul yom." And one also cannot say [he was] an intentional [transgressor], for we require that his statement be reconciled [with that claim]; had he said to them "I did not enter," he could have reconciled his statement [by explaining]: "I did not enter unwittingly, rather intentionally." However, since he said to them "I did not become impure," even if he says: "I did not become impure unwittingly, rather intentionally," he is not exempt from an offering, because with regard to impurity, it does not matter to us whether he was unwitting or intentional [when he contracted it], since [his] entry into the Temple was unwitting.

Rashi on Keritot 12a:7:1.english: You became impure - And you entered the Temple.

Rashi on Keritot 12a:7:2.hebrew: פטור - כדאמר לקמן: "והתודה" — מודה בדבר חייב, שאינו מודה בדבר פטור:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:7:2.english: Exempt - As it says below: "And he shall confess" [Leviticus 5:5] — one who confesses to the matter is liable [to bring an offering], [whereas] one who does not confess to the matter is exempt.

Rashi on Keritot 12a:8:1.english: Actually, the reason of the Rabbis is because of miggo - And it is regarding an old impurity that they disagree. We have the reading: "And this is what it teaches."

Rashi on Keritot 12a:8:2.hebrew: א"ה - גבי טומאה בהא פליגי, דר' מאיר לית ליה מיגו ורבנן אית להו מיגו, היינו חלב דמתני', ותרתי למה לי:
Rashi on Keritot 12a:8:2.english: If so - [that] regarding impurity they disagree about this, that Rabbi Meir does not hold [the principle of] miggo and the Rabbis do hold [the principle of] miggo, this is [identical to the case of] forbidden fat in our Mishnah, and why do I need both [cases]?

Rashi on Keritot 12a:9:1.hebrew: אכלת חלב - אית להו לרבנן מיגו משום דמתריץ דיבוריה כו', אבל טומאה, דליכא למימר "לא נטמאתי שוגג אלא מזיד", אימא לא מיתריץ דיבוריה. קמ"ל דמיתריץ בגוונא אחריתי: "לא עמדתי בטומאתי":
Rashi on Keritot 12a:9:1.english: You ate forbidden fat - The Rabbis hold [the principle of] migo because he explains his statement, etc. But [regarding] ritual impurity, where one cannot say, "I did not become impure unwittingly, rather intentionally," I might say his statement cannot be explained [away]. [The Gemara] teaches us that it is explained in a different manner: "I did not remain in my [state of] impurity."

Tosafot on Keritot 12a:12:1.hebrew: ומודים חכמים לר' יהודה בחלבין ובביאת מקדש אבל בטומאה לא מודו דפטור - רש"י פירש שתי לשונות, ור"י פירש שיטה אחרת: ומודים חכמים לר' יהודה כו' אבל בטומאה לא מודו ליה — כמו "נטמאת", והוא אמר "לא נטמאתי". ומפרש הש"ס: במאי? אילימא בטומאה ישנה, מ"ש הכא ומ"ש הכא?! אלא שמע מינה בטומאה חדשה, ומשום הכי לא מודו דלא שייך מיגו; וטעמייהו דרבנן משום מיגו, ודווקא בחלבים ובעריות מודו משום דשייך מיגו, אבל בטומאה לא מודו דלא שייך מיגו, אבל לר' יהודה דטעמא משום "אדם נאמן על כו'", פטר הכא והכא. ומיפשט בעיא דטעמייהו דרבנן דפליגי עליה דר"מ הוי מטעם מתרץ דיבוריה כדמשמע הכא, ואי רבנן דר"מ היינו רבי יהודה, טעמיה משום דאדם נאמן על עצמו. ודחי רבינא: לעולם אימא לך בטומאה ישנה; כלומר, מהכא לא מוכח מידי, דמצינו למימר דאפילו ר' יהודה לא מהימנא רק מטעם מיגו. והא דפליגי הכא בטומאה ישנה וקאמרי רבנן דחייב, כגון דקאמרי עדים "אכלת קדשים בטומאת הגוף", והוא אמר "לא נטמאתי" — דלא חשבי רבנן דמיתריץ דיבוריה בהא דאמר דר"ל "לא עמדתי בטומאתי אלא טבלתי"; דאי הוה אמר "לא אכלתי", מצינן למיתריץ דיבוריה שר"ל "לא עמדתי בטומאתי אלא טבלתי תחלה", אבל כשאומר "לא נטמאתי", כבר איתכחיש ליה מיגו קמא בטומאת מגע שאמר "לא נטמאתי", דמשמע לא שוגג ולא מזיד, כיון שלא השיב להם על האכילה כמו שאמרו לו. והך סוגיא דהכא קשה להא דפר"ק דבבא מציעא (דף ג:), דקאמר: לא תהא הודאת פיו גדולה מהעדאת עדים מק"ו; וקאמר: ק"ו, ומה פיו כו', ופריך: מה לפיו שכן מחייבו קרבן, תאמר בעדים שאין מחייבין אותו קרבן. ומאי פריך? הא דפיו מחייבו קרבן היינו כשאין עדים מכחישין — דאם אמר "אכלתי חלב בשוגג" והעדים מעידים שבאותו היום שאומר שאכל ובאותה שעה התרו בו, או שמעידין שהיה שומן, לא מחייב קרבן (מטותיה) [מפומיה] — ובעדים שאין פיו מכחישן חייב, דאפילו בעד אחד חייב, כדמשמע הכא! ועוד, אדרבה, עדים חמירי טפי מפיו, שהרי עדים מחייבין אותו אפילו פיו מכחישן, דעד כאן לא פטרי רבנן רק מטעם מיגו, אבל אי מכחיש להו בהדיא, חייב קרבן! ותו, מאי משני "ר' חייא כר"מ ס"ל"? אפילו כרבנן נמי, שהרי מחייבין היכא דלא מתרץ דיבוריה:
Tosafot on Keritot 12a:12:1.english: And the Sages concede to Rabbi Yehuda regarding [forbidden] fats and entering the Temple, but regarding ritual impurity they do not concede that he is exempt - Rashi explained two interpretations, and the Ri explained a different approach: "And the Sages concede to Rabbi Yehuda, etc., but regarding ritual impurity they do not concede to him" — such as [where witnesses say,] "You became impure," and he said, "I did not become impure." And the Talmud explains: With what [case are we dealing]? If we say [it is] with an old impurity, what is the difference here and what is the difference there?! Rather, infer from this [that it is dealing] with a new impurity, and for this reason they do not concede, because [the principle of] migo does not apply; for the Rabbis' reason is because of migo, and specifically regarding [forbidden] fats and forbidden sexual relations they concede because migo applies, whereas regarding ritual impurity they do not concede because migo does not apply; however, according to Rabbi Yehuda, whose reason is because "a person is believed regarding [himself], etc.," he exempts [him] both here and here. And [the Gemara initially thought] to resolve the dilemma [by concluding] that the reason of the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Meir is based on [the principle of] reconciling his words, as is implied here; and if the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Meir are [actually the view of] Rabbi Yehuda, his reason is because a person is believed regarding himself. And Ravina rejects [this]: Actually, I can say to you [that it is dealing] with an old impurity; that is to say, nothing is proven from here, for we can say that even Rabbi Yehuda [holds that] he is only believed on the basis of migo. And that which they disagree here regarding an old impurity and the Rabbis say that he is liable [is] such as where witnesses say, "You ate consecrated food in a state of bodily impurity," and he says, "I did not become impure" — for the Rabbis do not consider his words to be reconciled by this that he says, meaning to say, "I did not remain in my impurity, rather I immersed"; for had he said, "I did not eat," we could have reconciled his words [to mean] that he means to say, "I did not remain in my impurity, rather I immersed first," however, when he says, "I did not become impure," his first migo has already been contradicted regarding impurity of contact, since he said "I did not become impure," which implies neither unintentionally nor intentionally, since he did not respond to them regarding the eating as they said to him. And this sugya here is difficult [to reconcile] with that of the first chapter of Bava Metzia (3b), where it states: "The admission of his own mouth should not be greater than the testimony of witnesses, by an a fortiori argument"; and it states: "An a fortiori argument: If his own mouth, etc.," and it challenges [this]: "What is [unique] to his own mouth? That it obligates him [to bring] an offering! Will you say [the same] regarding witnesses, who do not obligate him [to bring] an offering?!" And why does it ask this challenge? For that [case where] his own mouth obligates him [to bring] an offering is [only] when witnesses do not contradict [him] — for if he said, "I ate forbidden fat unintentionally," and witnesses testify that on that very day that he says he ate and at that very hour they warned him [that it was forbidden], or they testify that it was [permitted] fat, he is not obligated [to bring] an offering from his own mouth — whereas with witnesses whom his mouth does not contradict, he is obligated, for even with one witness he is obligated, as is implied here! And furthermore, on the contrary, witnesses are more stringent than his own mouth, for witnesses obligate him even [when] his own mouth contradicts them, since thus far the Rabbis only exempt [him] on the basis of migo, but if he contradicts them explicitly, he is obligated [to bring] an offering! And furthermore, why does [the Gemara there] answer, "Rabbi Chiya holds in accordance with Rabbi Meir"? Even according to the Rabbis as well [witnesses obligate him], for they obligate [him] where he does not reconcile his words.

Tosafot on Keritot 12a:1:1.hebrew: אלא לאו בחד, וקתני כי אין מכחיש מהימן, ש"מ - אבל אי מכחיש לא מהימן. ור"ל ע"כ שאמר "איני יודע", דאי אמר בהדיא "לא אכלתי", פשיטא דפטור, דעד אחד אינו קם רק לשבועה, כדפרישית במתניתין:
Tosafot on Keritot 12a:1:1.english: "Rather, isn't [it referring] to one [witness], and it teaches that when he does not contradict [him], he is believed; learn from it" - However, if he contradicts [the witness], [the witness] is not believed. And [this] means perforce that he said, "I do not know," for if he said explicitly, "I did not eat [it]," it is obvious that he is exempt, since a single witness arises only [to obligate] an oath, as I explained on the Mishnah.

Tosafot on Keritot 12a:3:1.hebrew: או דלמא טעמייהו דרבנן משום מיגו דאי בעי אמר מזיד הייתי וכו' - משמע לפום ריהטא שהוא נאמן מטעם מיגו שיכול לומר מזיד (אני) הייתי. וקשה, שהרי מיגו במקום עדים הוא, דיש עדים שאכל והוא אמר: "לא אכלתי", וא"כ מהימנא ליה במקום עדים מכח מיגו! ואמרינן בב"מ (דף פא:): מיגו במקום עדים לא אמרינן, גבי ההיא ד"לא תיזיל באורחא דנהר פקוד זיל באורחא דנרש". ותו, אין זה מיגו, דלא משוי איניש נפשיה רשיעא, כדאמרינן (קדושין דף נ.) גבי ההיא: "הבא מן החלון", והביא לו מן הדלוסקמא (והביא לו), אע"פ שאומר בעל הבית: "לא היה בלבי מזה אלא מזה", בעל הבית כו' — דדברים שבלב אינן דברים; והתם מוכח ליה, ופריך: "ודלמא למיפטר נפשיה מקרבן קאמר?", ומשני: "דא"כ הוה אמר מזיד הייתי", ופריך: "והא לא משוי איניש נפשיה רשיעא!". לכך יש לומר, דהא דנאמן הכא, דמיתריץ דיבוריה, דאיכא למימר הא דאמר: "לא אכלתי" — רוצה לומר: "לא אכלתי שוגג, אלא מזיד". והכי פירושא: מיגו דאי בעי אמר: "מזיד הייתי" — פטור, השתא נמי מה שאמר: "לא אכלתי" — כך רצה לומר, והכי מתרצינן מילתיה דבהכי היה דעתו. ואף על גב דלא משוי איניש נפשיה רשיעא — כדאמר (סנהדרין דף ט:) גבי "פלוני רבעני", דאינו נאמן משום דאין אדם משים עצמו רשע — היינו ליפסל נפשיה לא מהימן, אבל אי אמר: "מזיד אכלתי חלב" — מהימן, דאומר מתכוין לטובה, שאינו רוצה להביא חולין בעזרה. וא"ת: ונישייליה אם היה דעתו לכך? ויש לומר, דאפי' הדר אמר הכי: "לא אכלתי שוגג אלא מזיד", כיון שלא אמר כך באותה שעה — מחייב ר"מ. והכי איתא בתורת כהנים: "אומר ר' מאיר: אם בתחלה אומר 'מזיד הייתי' — שומעין לו, אבל אם היה דן עמהם כל היום שאומר 'לא אכלתי' ולא אמר יותר, ואפילו אומר אח"כ 'לא אכלתי שוגג אלא מזיד' — חייב". וא"ת: היאך מחייב ר' מאיר, והאמר "לא אכלתי", ובע"כ לא יביא חטאת, כדאמר ב"ק (דף מ.): "חייבי חטאות אין ממשכנין אותן"? וי"ל, דהתם מיירי כשאמר דלא ניחא ליה בכפרה, אבל האי ניחא ליה בכפרה, אלא שהוא סבור להיות פטור — ממשכנין אותו:
Tosafot on Keritot 12a:3:1.english: Or perhaps the Rabbis' reasoning is because of miggo, [that] since if he wanted he could have said "I was intentional," etc. - It implies at first glance that he is believed on the basis of miggo, because he could say "I was intentional." And this is difficult, for it is a miggo against witnesses, since there are witnesses that he ate, and he said "I did not eat," and if so, we would be believing him against witnesses by force of miggo! Yet we say in Bava Metzia (81b) [that] we do not say miggo against witnesses, regarding that incident of "Do not go on the road of Nehar Pekod, go on the road of Naresh." Furthermore, this is not a [valid] miggo, because a person does not make himself out to be wicked, as we say (Kiddushin 50a) regarding that [case of] "Bring from the window" and he brought him from the chest (and he brought him), even though the homeowner says "I only had in mind from this [one] and not from that [one]," the homeowner etc. — for unspoken thoughts in the heart are not [legally significant] words; and there [the Gemara] proves [this], and asks: "Perhaps he says [this] to exempt himself from an offering?" And it answers: "Because if so, he would have said 'I was intentional.'" And it asks: "But a person does not make himself out to be wicked!" Therefore, one must say that the reason he is believed here is that his statement is interpreted favorably, for one can say [that] when he said "I did not eat," he meant to say "I did not eat unintentionally, rather intentionally." And this is the explanation: Since (miggo) if he wanted he could have said "I was intentional" [and] been exempt, now too, what he said "I did not eat" — this is what he meant to say, and thus we interpret his words, that this was his intention. And even though a person does not make himself out to be wicked — as it says (Sanhedrin 9b) regarding [one who says] "So-and-so sodomized me," that he is not believed because a person does not make himself out to be wicked — that is [only] to disqualify himself [as a witness] that he is not believed; but if he says "I ate forbidden fat intentionally," he is believed, because he says [it] intending [something] good, [namely] that he does not want to bring unconsecrated animals into the Temple Courtyard. And if you ask: Let us ask him if that was his intention? One can say that even if he goes back and says thus: "I did not eat unintentionally, rather intentionally," since he did not say so at that time, Rabbi Meir holds him liable. And so it is [taught] in Torat Kohanim: "Rabbi Meir says: If at the outset he says 'I was intentional,' we listen to him; but if he was arguing with them all day, saying 'I did not eat,' and did not say anything more, then even if he says afterward 'I did not eat unintentionally, rather intentionally,' he is liable." And if you ask: How does Rabbi Meir hold him liable, when he said "I did not eat," and against his will he will not bring a sin-offering, as it says in Bava Kamma (40a): "Those obligated [to bring] sin-offerings are not forced via collateral"? One can answer that there it is referring to when he said that he does not desire atonement; but this one [here] desires atonement, except that he thinks he is exempt — [so] we do force him via collateral.

Tosafot on Keritot 12a:4:1.hebrew: נפקא מינה לטומאה - וה"נ מצי למימר: נפקא מינה היכא שאמר "לא אכלתי, לא שוגג ולא מזיד":
Tosafot on Keritot 12a:4:1.english: A practical difference for impurity - And similarly, [the Gemara] could have said [that] there is a practical difference where he said, "I did not eat, neither unwittingly nor intentionally."
